Definition: from G4862 and G5055; to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively):--end, finish, fulfil, make.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus is forty days tempted of the devil, and when the days are ended He hungers, and the Lord says the days come when He will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. The ending of the forty days brings hunger, and the coming of the new covenant brings a new beginning, and both are the completing of what God set out to do.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God completes what He begins, whether it is forty days of temptation or a new covenant, and I hold that the end of the trial is the start of the promise.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
